The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: a first run to value journey on this page, walked as this persona, reaches value without a dead end
evidence.checked: PASSES: reached value: 1167 chars, 8 actionable control(s), 0 stuck skeletons, 0 failed read(s). PERSONA: this row was walked as "project manager" (slot P1), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'supervisor'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. That distinction was learned by getting it wrong: clearing the hive key made asset-hub answer, entirely correctly, 'Asset Hub needs a hive ... Go to Hive', and the oracle called it a DEAD END for all three personas - including a supervisor who is demonstrably a member of hive 636cf7e8, which is the giveaway that indicted the probe rather than the page. Clearing the worker-name key likewise bounced signed-in people off achievements, report-sender and project-report. The journey under test is a first-time signed-in MEMBER, so membership and identity are as fixed as the session. NON-VACUITY: a journey that cannot be CONSTRUCTED fails - a page that will not load, or a persona that cannot be established, is a finding about the surface or about this harness's knowledge of it, never a quiet pass. This is the discipline the marketplace spec tests/ux-journeys.spec.ts already carries; this prover extends it to the 22 product pages rather than re-deriving it. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT, and the specific lie this oracle is built to refuse: A FIRST-RUN SCREEN CAN BE A LIE. This platform has already shipped a page (skillmatrix) that asked a worker to re-pick a discipline they had already chosen, because the READ had failed and the page rendered its first-run onboarding as the fallback. To a naive 'did the person reach something actionable?' check that scores as a PASS - there is content, there are buttons, there is a clear next step - while it is the OPPOSITE of value: it invites the person to redo setup they already did, and can overwrite it. So reaching an onboarding screen is credited as value ONLY if the page's own reads SUCCEEDED, counted from the network (4xx/5xx on /rest/v1, /rpc, /functions/v1), not guessed. Onboarding over a failed read is banked as a FAILURE with its status codes. That is the A16.P7 mechanism rule: credit the right cause, not merely the observed property. A dead end (<3 visible actionable controls, or <300 characters) fails. A still-shimmering VISIBLE skeleton after 7.6s fails - a page that never resolves is not value, and only visible skeletons count because a hidden template is not a state. For two_context, BOTH identities must reach value; one succeeding while the other dead-ends is a failure. J2 repeat_visit is measured as a DELTA, in the same session, where the only thing that changed is that the person has been here before. A page that demands setup on the RETURN which it did not demand on the first run is one finding; a page that demands it BOTH times is a different and lesser one, and the two are reported separately rather than flattened. 'Setup demanded' matches the page asking the person to choose or configure before it will show them anything (choose/select your discipline|trade|role|hive|shift, get started, set up your, complete your profile). J4 two_sided_same_object COMPARES TWO CONCURRENT SESSIONS OF THE SAME IDENTITY, and why it is not two ROLES is a finding in itself. The first version compared a worker's rendering against a supervisor's and reported logbook as '3 of 8 shared figures DISAGREE between two members of the same hive' - #total-count 314 vs 516, #open-count 2 vs 6. Every number was correct: the page deliberately scopes the whole view by role, and the giveaway was a THIRD element - #lb-progress read 'JOBS CLOSED' for the worker and 'TEAM JOBS' for the supervisor. Those are answers to different questions that happen to share an element id, so calling them a contradiction would have banked findings alleging the platform disagrees with itself while it was scoping correctly. Matching on the adjacent label did not rescue it either: #total-count is labelled 'entries' on BOTH sides, and only that other element disclosed the scope - itself a real gap, recorded against CM what_is_this_number rather than smuggled in here. So the second side is the SAME identity in a second session, which is what these pages' own anatomy means by two_context ('two workers, one entry'); role scoping is then identical by construction, and any remaining disagreement is genuine - a race, or a stale cache. Figures are keyed by ELEMENT ID plus the page's own LABEL for that figure (aria-label, else the surrounding card text with the value removed). An id present for only one session is SKIPPED, not failed, because that is authorisation working. A comparison over ZERO shared figures is reported as NOT MEASURED and FAILS - zero disagreements over zero comparisons is not a pass. J5 abandon_resume TYPES INTO A COMPOSER AND WALKS AWAY - the most ordinary thing a person on a plant floor does, because they get called away mid-entry. A marker string is typed into the first visible text field of the page's own dialog (opened via tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the SAME grounded table four other provers read, so this cannot drift from how those views are known to open), the walker then leaves the page entirely and returns. THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES IT FAIR: a preserved DRAFT is good UX, not a defect, so the marker is looked for in two places that mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD = a draft was kept, which PASSES and is noted as deliberate. Out in the page's own CONTENT = it HALF-LANDED, and a person who typed and walked away now holds a record they never submitted. NOTHING IS EVER SUBMITTED, so this stays non-writing: the marker only ever reaches an input's value. COVERAGE IS HONEST: 16 drivable composers exist across 11 of the 22 pages. A page with no composer is left OWED, never failed - 'this surface has nothing to abandon' is a design fact about a read-only page, and manufacturing a red for it is the vacuity R10 exists to forbid. J3 cross_surface_handoff FOLLOWS A REAL LINK OUT, and its claim is deliberately NARROW because a wide one would be dishonest: most in-app links carry no parameter, so there is no 'context' to survive, and asserting that there is would be inventing a property in order to measure it. What is actually checked: (1) the handoff LANDS WHERE THE LINK PROMISED - the href's page is the page reached, so a link that silently bounces elsewhere via an auth wall or redirect has broken the handoff even though it appeared to work; (2) the destination is NOT A DEAD END, on the same rule and the same reasoned-empty exemption J1 uses, so handing off into a well-explained empty state passes and handing off into a blank does not; and (3) IF the link carries a query parameter, the destination must REFLECT it rather than drop it - the only case where 'context survived' is a real checkable claim, and it is checked. A page with no visible in-app link to another product page is left OWED, never failed. SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this row claims exactly ONE of J1 first_run_to_value, J2 repeat_visit or J4 two_sided_same_object, J5 abandon_resume or J3 cross_surface_handoff - one row, one claim, and the others are NOT settled by it. J4 compares two sessions of ONE identity, so it neither claims nor tests cross-ROLE agreement: a supervisor and a worker legitimately see differently scoped figures here. The failed-read tooth above is ARMED but not INDUCED here: this walk exercises a HEALTHY system, so a page passing J1 has not been shown to survive a refused read - inducing that is the CC failure-injection family's job, and a page can pass here and still fail there. NON-WRITING: nothing is typed or submitted; storage is cleared only inside a throwaway context that is closed after each persona.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

On this page the person-caused action is drafting the AI narrative, which is ONE press - there is no part-way. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: a first run to value journey on this page, walked as this persona, reaches value without a dead end
evidence.checked: PASSES: reached value: 1167 chars, 8 actionable control(s), 0 stuck skeletons, 0 failed read(s). PERSONA: this row was walked as "member" (slot P2), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'worker'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. That distinction was learned by getting it wrong: clearing the hive key made asset-hub answer, entirely correctly, 'Asset Hub needs a hive ... Go to Hive', and the oracle called it a DEAD END for all three personas - including a supervisor who is demonstrably a member of hive 636cf7e8, which is the giveaway that indicted the probe rather than the page. Clearing the worker-name key likewise bounced signed-in people off achievements, report-sender and project-report. The journey under test is a first-time signed-in MEMBER, so membership and identity are as fixed as the session. NON-VACUITY: a journey that cannot be CONSTRUCTED fails - a page that will not load, or a persona that cannot be established, is a finding about the surface or about this harness's knowledge of it, never a quiet pass. This is the discipline the marketplace spec tests/ux-journeys.spec.ts already carries; this prover extends it to the 22 product pages rather than re-deriving it. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT, and the specific lie this oracle is built to refuse: A FIRST-RUN SCREEN CAN BE A LIE. This platform has already shipped a page (skillmatrix) that asked a worker to re-pick a discipline they had already chosen, because the READ had failed and the page rendered its first-run onboarding as the fallback. To a naive 'did the person reach something actionable?' check that scores as a PASS - there is content, there are buttons, there is a clear next step - while it is the OPPOSITE of value: it invites the person to redo setup they already did, and can overwrite it. So reaching an onboarding screen is credited as value ONLY if the page's own reads SUCCEEDED, counted from the network (4xx/5xx on /rest/v1, /rpc, /functions/v1), not guessed. Onboarding over a failed read is banked as a FAILURE with its status codes. That is the A16.P7 mechanism rule: credit the right cause, not merely the observed property. A dead end (<3 visible actionable controls, or <300 characters) fails. A still-shimmering VISIBLE skeleton after 7.6s fails - a page that never resolves is not value, and only visible skeletons count because a hidden template is not a state. For two_context, BOTH identities must reach value; one succeeding while the other dead-ends is a failure. J2 repeat_visit is measured as a DELTA, in the same session, where the only thing that changed is that the person has been here before. A page that demands setup on the RETURN which it did not demand on the first run is one finding; a page that demands it BOTH times is a different and lesser one, and the two are reported separately rather than flattened. 'Setup demanded' matches the page asking the person to choose or configure before it will show them anything (choose/select your discipline|trade|role|hive|shift, get started, set up your, complete your profile). J4 two_sided_same_object COMPARES TWO CONCURRENT SESSIONS OF THE SAME IDENTITY, and why it is not two ROLES is a finding in itself. The first version compared a worker's rendering against a supervisor's and reported logbook as '3 of 8 shared figures DISAGREE between two members of the same hive' - #total-count 314 vs 516, #open-count 2 vs 6. Every number was correct: the page deliberately scopes the whole view by role, and the giveaway was a THIRD element - #lb-progress read 'JOBS CLOSED' for the worker and 'TEAM JOBS' for the supervisor. Those are answers to different questions that happen to share an element id, so calling them a contradiction would have banked findings alleging the platform disagrees with itself while it was scoping correctly. Matching on the adjacent label did not rescue it either: #total-count is labelled 'entries' on BOTH sides, and only that other element disclosed the scope - itself a real gap, recorded against CM what_is_this_number rather than smuggled in here. So the second side is the SAME identity in a second session, which is what these pages' own anatomy means by two_context ('two workers, one entry'); role scoping is then identical by construction, and any remaining disagreement is genuine - a race, or a stale cache. Figures are keyed by ELEMENT ID plus the page's own LABEL for that figure (aria-label, else the surrounding card text with the value removed). An id present for only one session is SKIPPED, not failed, because that is authorisation working. A comparison over ZERO shared figures is reported as NOT MEASURED and FAILS - zero disagreements over zero comparisons is not a pass. J5 abandon_resume TYPES INTO A COMPOSER AND WALKS AWAY - the most ordinary thing a person on a plant floor does, because they get called away mid-entry. A marker string is typed into the first visible text field of the page's own dialog (opened via tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the SAME grounded table four other provers read, so this cannot drift from how those views are known to open), the walker then leaves the page entirely and returns. THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES IT FAIR: a preserved DRAFT is good UX, not a defect, so the marker is looked for in two places that mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD = a draft was kept, which PASSES and is noted as deliberate. Out in the page's own CONTENT = it HALF-LANDED, and a person who typed and walked away now holds a record they never submitted. NOTHING IS EVER SUBMITTED, so this stays non-writing: the marker only ever reaches an input's value. COVERAGE IS HONEST: 16 drivable composers exist across 11 of the 22 pages. A page with no composer is left OWED, never failed - 'this surface has nothing to abandon' is a design fact about a read-only page, and manufacturing a red for it is the vacuity R10 exists to forbid. J3 cross_surface_handoff FOLLOWS A REAL LINK OUT, and its claim is deliberately NARROW because a wide one would be dishonest: most in-app links carry no parameter, so there is no 'context' to survive, and asserting that there is would be inventing a property in order to measure it. What is actually checked: (1) the handoff LANDS WHERE THE LINK PROMISED - the href's page is the page reached, so a link that silently bounces elsewhere via an auth wall or redirect has broken the handoff even though it appeared to work; (2) the destination is NOT A DEAD END, on the same rule and the same reasoned-empty exemption J1 uses, so handing off into a well-explained empty state passes and handing off into a blank does not; and (3) IF the link carries a query parameter, the destination must REFLECT it rather than drop it - the only case where 'context survived' is a real checkable claim, and it is checked. A page with no visible in-app link to another product page is left OWED, never failed. SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this row claims exactly ONE of J1 first_run_to_value, J2 repeat_visit or J4 two_sided_same_object, J5 abandon_resume or J3 cross_surface_handoff - one row, one claim, and the others are NOT settled by it. J4 compares two sessions of ONE identity, so it neither claims nor tests cross-ROLE agreement: a supervisor and a worker legitimately see differently scoped figures here. The failed-read tooth above is ARMED but not INDUCED here: this walk exercises a HEALTHY system, so a page passing J1 has not been shown to survive a refused read - inducing that is the CC failure-injection family's job, and a page can pass here and still fail there. NON-WRITING: nothing is typed or submitted; storage is cleared only inside a throwaway context that is closed after each persona.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.
